newsitem.title: GERMANY: C&W could decide next week on German deal.
newsitem.headline: C&W could decide next week on German deal.

text.p: European telecommunications alliances may be on the verge of a major shake-up that could have a huge impact in Germany and shift the power balance in the global telecoms market, industry officials said on Saturday.

Cable and Wireless (C&W), the international telecoms group, has been holding up a final agreement to bring German utility RWE AG into its alliance with utility Veba AG as it reassesses its global strategy, they said.
Officials at C&W and Veba confirmed contracts to conclude the deal had not been signed and that talks were continuing.
"We are working with Veba and RWE to bring RWE into the alliance," a C&W spokeswoman said in response to a report in the Financial Times newspaper that negotiations about the deal had been reopened.

Officials at the German utilities said a decision about whether C&W remains in the alliance or abandons its European partners to pursue Asian and U.S. activities could be decided in a round of tense meetings in Germany in the coming days.
"It could all be decided in the next week," a Veba official told Reuters.

The three-party alliance is one of several large telecoms ventures gearing up to compete with former communications monopolies when Europe drops the final barriers to full competition in the sector next year.
C&W and Veba formed a strategic alliance in 1995, with Veba taking a 10.5 percent stake in the British telecoms group and C&W taking 45 percent of a joint venture called Vebacom GmbH.
Last year, the two companies agreed to bring RWE on board and after months of negotiations drew up the final contracts two weeks ago. But C&W has declined to sign them.

It has been exploring the possibility of a new strategic alliance with one of its main international competitors, the Global One venture of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint Corp, officials said.
"Cable and Wireless has held talks with Global One and it is not clear yet what they will do," an RWE official said.
Officials at the German utilities said C&W chief executive Richard Brown has for now stopped further investment in Europe.
C&W now had to decide either to go forward with the alliance, which would mean sinking more cash in Germany to keep its stake at current levels, or to bid farewell to its partners and move on.
"Either they will stay or they will go. There is no in between," one German industry official said.
The German utilities believe that Brown, a former Sprint executive, was shifting Cable and Wireless's international strategy to focus more on the United States and Asia.

C&W and Global One would fit well together. C&W has a strong presence in Asia with its holdings in Hong Kong Telecom, and its Mercury subsidiary in Britain would also give Global One a beachhead to battle British Telecom.

C&W, which operates a global optical fibre backbone network but has been seen as lacking direction in its global strategy, would benefit significantly from the strong position in Europe of the French and German telecoms and Sprint's U.S. presence.
Such an alliance could finally create a global telecoms group with a strong presence in the U.S., Europe and Asia and increase Global One's attraction to multinational businesses.

The talks with Global One coincide with talks between British Telecom and Japan's NTT. Both companies have played down their meetings, but speculation persists that they could produce some form of cooperation.
Industry analysts say it remains unclear how AT&T Corp plans to fill the gaps in its European and Asian expansion strategies as it appears to fall further behind the BT/MCI Concert alliance.
-- Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150
